transcript.text: My Samsung dishwasher DW60M6050FS keeps showing 4C and beeping, won't do anything

The '4C' code on Samsung dishwashers typically indicates a water supply issue – the machine isn't detecting that fresh water is entering within the expected time. This is often caused by the tap being off, a kinked inlet hose, or a blockage in the filter. First, please check if the water tap supplying the dishwasher is fully open and whether the inlet hose at the back of the machine is straight and not kinked. Let me know what you find.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
Checked the hose and it's not kinked. The valve under the sink is a screwdriver-slot one and the slot is at 90 degrees, so I think it's turned off. Should I turn it on?

[Heading: Water supply valve closed]
Yes, please turn that valve on. For most screwdriver-slot valves, the slot being parallel with the pipe means it is open (90 degrees usually means closed). Once you've turned it fully on, try to start a programme again. If the 4C code disappears and the machine starts filling, we're done. If the error returns even though the valve is open, let me know.
Ok, I've turned the valve on and started a programme again. It's filling now and running normally, so that fixed it. The plumber was working under the sink yesterday so he must have turned it off.
That's excellent news. The '4C' code was indeed caused by the water supply being cut off while the plumber worked under the sink. You can leave the valve in that open position for normal use.
